name: Generic Tree Traversal - Pre And Post Order
html:
Hey coder. We start with our new question "Traversals in Generic Tree" where we are going to discuss Pre-order and Post-order traversals.

This is a great question to get in depth knowledge on how traversals work which will be beneficial for understanding other questions as well.

If you haven't watched the question video yet, we suggest you watch it now.

Important Links : Question Video, Solution Video

Problem Discussion : Watch video

If we are given an input tree as shown in Figure 1,then,

some of the positions during Euler traversal are shown in Figure 2.

For elements, say parent 10 and child 20,

  1. When we traverse through the left of an element, we print "Node Pre 10".
  2. When we traverse through the left edge between two elements we print "Edge Pre 10--20".
  3. When we traverse through the right of an element, we print "Node Post 10".
  4. When we traverse through the right edge between two elements we print "Edge Post 10--20".
Approach :
  • Pre - Order Traversal-
    1. When we are anywhere to the left of an element, it is called Pre - Order Traversal.
    2. It is written before the recursive call is made.
    3. This takes place while going up the stack.
    4. Root is visited before visiting its children.
  • Post - Order Traversal-
    1. Whenever we are at the right of an element, it is called Post - Order Traversal.
    2. It is written after the recursive call is made.
    3. This takes place while going down the stack.
    4. Root is visited after visiting its children.

You can also watch the solution video to review these traversals.

Watch video

We now try to imagine the required areas to be printed with the help of the following code.

public static void traversals(Node node){ //Euler's Left/ Node Pre/ Into the recursion System.out.println("Node Pre "+node.data); for(Node child: node.children) { //Edge Pre System.out.println("Edge Pre "+node.data+"--"+child.data); traversals(child); System.out.println("Edge Post "+node.data+"--"+child.data); //Edge Post } System.out.println("Node Post "+node.data); //Euler's right/Node Post/on the way out of recursion }
java; true";

We have distinctly mentioned all the areas we are supposed to print using comments in the above code.

These areas show if they are defined before or after a line of code.

We highly suggest you first try to dry run this code yourself, print the output and then check out the solution video.

Watch video Analysis: Time Complexity:

O(2n)

Space Complexity:

O(1)

Since no extra space is used in the program, therefore the space complexity is constant. This complexity is not including the space required for the recursion stack.

OUTPUT

The output for our code for the given input tree should be:

Node Pre 10
Edge Pre 10--20
Node Pre 20
Node Post 20
Edge Post 10--20
Edge Pre 10--30
Node Pre 30
Edge Pre 30--50
Node Pre 50
Node Post 50
Edge Post 30--50
Edge Pre 30--60
Node Pre 60
Node Post 60
Edge Post 30--60
Node Post 30
Edge Post 10--30
Edge Pre 10--40
Node Pre 40
Node Post 40
Edge Post 10--40
Node Post 10



With this we conclude this question. We'll see you in the upcoming questions.
